messages:
maria: Quick sync — starting a coordinated driver/firmware/kernel validation this week for eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Goal: reduce XID/ECC spike frequency (aiming for ~60% drop vs current baseline). Need a short burn-in plan + canary criteria.
kevin: Can do. Proposal: 50-node burn-in per region, 48h for older cards (p40/p80), 24h for p4 family. I have a job YAML ready.
nash: @kevin can you include a mixed-sequence workload (chat gen + batching) so we exercise KV cache paths?
maria: yes, include both seq-len 256 and 2048 runs. Also add a small mem/IO stress to surface ECC faults.
kevin: uploaded job snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: fw-burnin-canary-1842109876
  labels:
    test: fw_canary_v2
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        gpu-family: mixed
      containers:
      - name: burnin
        image: redwood/gpu-burnin:stable
        args: ["--workloads=gen,kvcache,memtest","--duration=48h"]
```
ashley: We should test kernel 5.15.128 and 6.1.52 with drivers 525.116 & 535.86 and NV firmware revs 94 & 98. Run pairwise so we can isolate which layer helps.
dinesh: I'll add tracepoints and telemetry tag `fw_canary_v2` to GPU metrics and increase metrics scrape to 10s for the canary. Also will attach dmesg + `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots every 5m.
ci-bot: ci-bot: Canary job scheduled: job/driver-fw-burnin-1842109876 in eu-west-1 pool
kevin: 12h status: eu-west-1: 0 XIDs across 50 nodes. us-west-2: 3 XIDs on 10 nodes, all on host-23 (same rack). Flagging as possible riser/hw fault rather than driver.
nash: good catch — I'll put host-23 into drain and kick a repro on a spare in a different rack.
dinesh: requesting `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ELP` dump from the affected host, and please paste last 200 lines of dmesg. Example command: `sudo nvidia-smi -q -x | tee /tmp/gpu-q.xml`
maria: pls keep all logs in /var/log/gpu-health/fw_canary_v2/ and tag any drained hosts with `drain-firmware-triage`. Add host annotations to fleet DB.
kevin: cost note: 50-node x 48h burn-in across two regions ~= $Xk. If we trust p4 family, we can cut to 24h there and save ~40%. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
nash: :+1: 24h p4, 48h older cards sounds reasonable. For older cards we have more historic flakiness.
maria: OK sticking with that. Rollout criteria: if aggregated XID rate <= baseline*0.4 across both regions and no new ECC errors after 72h, schedule staged rollout 10% -> 30% -> 100% over Dedicated pools with 24h observation windows. If any host shows >5 XIDs/hr during burn-in, automatically drain and replace.
kevin: I'll add an automatic rollback to previous driver if XID>threshold and notify #eng-oncall.
dinesh: will produce a small post-run report: XID counts, ECC corrected/uncorrected, host-level notes, dmesg excerpts, and suggested kernel/driver combo. ETA 72h after start.
maria: thanks — ping me when the post-run report is up. If the canary looks clean we'll prep release notes and ops runbook for rollout.
